The HARD known set on the chain head after this ruling is enumerated for condition (c)'s re-run: citation_sweep 10 problems (P01-012 refs[1] under S1-06; P02-013 ידעתם; the eight pointed S1-07 splices P03-004, P03-005 x2, P03-006, P03-010, P03-012, P03-017, P03-019) and the normalizer's 8 distinct defect runs (9 listed, P03-005's run twice). Recommendation for Daniel's writer brief, not an order: an unpointed Hebrew run in prose is a whole word of a nearby cited verse; a formula family or root is labelled by the whole word the cited verse writes, or is cited beside a verse that writes the bare form.
rulings.reason: Bytes: MT 12:20's seventh word is וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם, code points U+05D5 U+05B4 U+05BD U+05D9 U+05D3 U+05B7 U+05E2 U+05B0 U+05EA U+05B6 U+05BC U+0596 U+05DD; the conjunction vav (U+05D5) is the word's first letter, so the skeleton whole word is וידעתם and ידעתם is that word minus its first letter. The row's sentence uses ידעתם as a label ('part of the wider 21-verse ידעתם recognition family') beside a verbatim pointed quote of 12:20 and a ref to it, while the row's own refs entry already writes the family word as the verse does: 'oshb:Ezek.12.20 (recognition.2mp family — וידעתם, sweep: 21 verses book-wide, not the strict 28)'. Book-wide, bare ידעתם stands as a whole word in exactly two verses (17:12 הלא ידעתם מה אלה and 32:9 אשר לא ידעתם, neither a recognition-formula verse) while וידעתם stands as a whole word in 25; the label as written is neither what 12:20 says nor the form the family carries. Corpus measure (whatif.json W4): of the 52 unpointed runs of 3+ letters in the chain head's prose, 51 are whole words at their nearest cited verse under rule A; the class is one run and the fix is one word (וידעתם, matching refs[1]) in a part already in FIXUP-1. Rule C would add a letter-class heuristic (ו ב כ ל מ ה ש, up to two) to a HARD gate to save that one word, with a residual no test closes: at the skeleton tier a stem letter from the same set (מ in משפט or מדבר, ש in שאול) is indistinguishable from a proclitic, so a root cited inside a derived noun would pass; narrowing to real proclitic stacks (ו + one; ב כ ל מ + ה) buys nothing on that residual, because ומשפט still reads as ו + מ + שפט. Rule B drops the skeleton half of S1-07 outright (the ezek_lib 'root' selftest case would have to go). My #e4 unresolved_uncertainty[1] reserved narrowing 'if the bytes warrant it'; the bytes show a class of one that the rows' own practice already avoids. Pointed runs keep the byte-class boundary under every option, so the S1-07 class (8 grapheme-cut splices) is untouched. The ref arm is consistent with this: refs[1]'s וידעתם collates as a whole word at 12:20, and the corpus-impact report lists only P01-012 under S1-06.

W5 ADOPTED in this implementable form: in rule 4's backward scan a negator distributes across a comma list when its own comma-delimited segment is the negator plus at most two words, every intervening segment is at most two words and names no verse, and the token's segment begins with the token (optionally after and/or/nor). Its residual - an off-by-one claim 'a samekh follows 36:13' passing when the mark is after 36:12 - is a lost FLAGS triage item, not a HARD hole, and rule 2 symmetry still flags an undisclosed 36:12 unless the row names it within 160 characters of a mark word. The three W1 keeps: P02-002 x2 are a true absence claim in the letter-name form the ABSENCE regex does not know (hence W6); P11-012 is a semantic claim about a different type, and W1 rightly keeps it. W2: the six removals are non-absence uses of a K/Q token - a splicing description ('not the whole-verse ketiv/qere concatenation', two tokens), 'never argued from any of these Qere readings', 'no measurement digit ... both K/Q verses', P02-020's Qere-adaptation sentence, and P10-008's exclusivity claim - and the two keeps are byte-false. On 'other': S1-08 found P10-008's exclusivity claim byte-false against the notes_other layer and #e4 FIXUP-1 already orders that sentence dropped; an exclusivity claim is exactly the sentence this arm exists to test, so exempting it loses the one check that matters, while checking it against the span's every kq key flags every honest 'no other' beside a disclosed one - the difference is the disclosed keys, which the row names. P10-008 names oshb:Ezek.41.15 in its rationale and 'K/Q at 41:15' in device_notes, so under the amended rule its flag is removed on the merits, not by exemption. W5: the three clauses are true - pmarks holds no mark and no kq key in MT 40:17-40:19, 40:38-40:47 or 40:48-41:4, checked key by key - and the comma-cut negator is a parsing artefact of NEG_CLAUSE_END; the implementable form refuses distribution when the negator's segment is itself a clause ('No parashah stands here, K/Q at N is disclosed' stays a positive claim over N). W6: ABSENCE's alternatives name petuchah|setumah|parashah|paragraph mark and never pe|samekh, so rule 1 reads 'no pe or samekh follows 8:13' as two positive claims; neither 8:12 nor 8:13 carries a mark, so W1 keeps both flags; the same MARKISH_CTX gate that admits the letter names as mark words keeps W6 out of letter talk. check_marks is a FLAGS member: every change here moves triage, never a HARD verdict.

(2) 'previously held' is narrowed to the repair-narration shape S1 quoted: \bpreviously (?:held|drafted|spanned|read) as\b. Adopted as proposed: \bprior [\w:.\-–]+(?: [\w:.\-–]+)? reading\b and \bformer (?:[\w.\-–]+ ){0,2}(?:span|row)\b. GREEN controls required in section 10b beside the ruling's two: 'the former kings', 'the last of the gates', 'one of three rows of chambers', 'the land previously held by Judah', 'the prior verse'. RED vectors: 'keeping the prior 28:24-26 reading', 'its former nineteen-verse span', 'the former single 48.1-29 span', 'the last of three land_allotment rows', 'ground previously held as one 29-verse row'.
